To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
LTR-retroelements are the most abundant class of transposable element in the oil palm and that they are not currently active in the genomes of E. guineenses and E. oleifer.
LTR-retroelement content of the two oil palm genomes is similar, with a high proportion of Copia elements.

(i) we identified and described a large number of LTR retroelements in both E. oleiferra and E. guinenesis genomes, and (ii) we showed that the retrotransposition activity of these elements is no longer active in these genomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the LTR retrotransposable elements of the oil palm, which will be a key resource for the understanding of the genome composition and evolution of these palms.
the identification of LTR-retroposons in the genomes of oil palm, their annotation, and their comparative analysis between the genomes of E. oleiferra and E. guinensis.
the identification of LTR retroelement sequences, their annotation and the analysis of their genomic distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LTR retrotransposable elements are the major components of the oil palm genome.
the oil palm genome is highly repetitive, with a high proportion of retrotransposon content and that this content is similar between the two Elaeis species.
the LTR retrotransposable elements are not only a major part of the genome, they are also a major part of its history and evolution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LTR-retroelement landscape in oil palm is characterized by a high proportion of L1 retrotransposons and by a high diversity and abundance of LTR retroelements.
the oil palm genome is rich in retrotransposons.

LTR retrotransposition has shaped oil palm genome organization and evolution, and that it is a valuable resource for improving genome annotation and investigating the evolutionary history of this species.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, although the genomes of both species are very different, the TE content of the two genomes is very similar.
LTR retrotransposition has played a major role in shaping the genome of both oil palms and that this process has occurred in both species in the same way.
LTR-retroelements in the Elaeiseae lineage have a common origin and have been subject to a similar evolutionary fate.
